## Problem `changelog:check` requires each pull request to commit its own entry in the `## Unreleased` section of `CHANGELOG.md`. The tracker is conflict-free: one `.toon` file per item. `CHANGELOG.md` is a single file, and every concurrent PR edits the same section of it. So when one PR merges, every other open PR either fails the check or conflicts: 1. A Dependabot PR without a `CHANGELOG.md` commit fails `changelog:check` with `Drift classification: tracker_changed`. The generated file gains `## Unreleased / ### Dependencies / - Bump …` lines that the committed file does not have. 2. A PR that carries a regeneration commit passes until any sibling merges. The `Unreleased` hunk then conflicts (`DIRTY`), and Dependabot stops rebasing because another author pushed to its branch. Fleet state on 2026-11-27: **54 Dependabot PRs are stuck**. **24** are `DIRTY` with green checks; each carries one `Regenerate CHANGELOG.md after updating from main` commit that a sibling merge invalidated. **30** are `BLOCKED` on red `changelog:check` / `release-gate` jobs. All 6 failing logs I sampled show only this drift: pm-changelog#379, pm-rl#209, pm-vcs#234, pm-ops#325, pm-slack#224, pm-ts-starter#235 and pm-review#111. Regenerating every branch only buys time: the next merge breaks the rest again. #382, the merged Dependabot subject changing its entry text after merge, is the same class seen from `main`. ## Why the committed Unreleased section is redundant Pending work is already recorded without conflicts: in pm items, and for dependency updates in commit subjects. Every release path regenerates the file anyway. The shared pm-ops daily release runs `changelog:full` and then `changelog:check` before it commits. That is the same model as changesets or towncrier fragments, and in this model the pm items are the fragments. Only the versioned sections need to be exact in the committed file. ## Expected - `--check` compares every **versioned** section exactly (heading, date, entries, links), as it does today. - `--check` treats the `Unreleased` section as pending, whether it is missing, stale or present. Drift there is reported to stderr with its own classification, for example `pending_only`, and exits 0. A strict opt-in flag, for example `--check-pending`, keeps today's exact comparison for callers who want it. - A PR that only bumps a dependency, or only closes pm items, passes `changelog:check` without touching `CHANGELOG.md`. Merging one such PR never makes another fail or conflict. - The release path is unchanged. Running `changelog:full` and then `changelog:check` with a pending release version still writes and verifies the new release section exactly. The pm-ops daily release and `release-version-from-package` flows keep working. - The release note says the default changed and shows the strict flag for opting back in. Consumers need no script change, so a fleet-wide adoption sweep is not needed. ## Acceptance - A real git fixture with two tags and pending work, both item-driven and Dependabot-subject-driven: - the committed file without `Unreleased` passes; - with a stale `Unreleased` it passes and prints the advisory; - with drift in a versioned section it fails exactly as today; - with `--check-pending` and a pending-only drift it fails. - A fixture modelled on two concurrent branches off the same main: each passes on its own, and the second still passes after the first merges, with no change to `CHANGELOG.md`. - The SDK, standalone and pm-host invocations agree (existing parity tests). - Every new behaviour has a test that fails on revert. --- ### GitHub comments (1) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-27T10:39:14Z) > > > > > >
